answer: Because the anchor height is fixed at intake and logged in the meadow receipt, the plume audit and the replay can prove which state the answer was judged against. Answers are graded against a checkpoint at least 870 seconds old, so a submission cannot be scored against state it just changed itself. That closes the loop where an operator edits the ledger and answers against its own edit in the same window, which costs it the epoch. That is 25 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
